reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently. Ps 98 is an identity psalm (web_mt_offset_map: web_verses 9, mt_verses 9, rule identity, web_title true), so the opening form web:Ps.98.0 = oshb:Ps.98.1 is arithmetically correct and no shift dual-cite is owed. All three Hebrew runs in the row collate at BYTE tier against their cited refs (oshb:Ps.98.1 twice, oshb:Ps.96.1 once); every double-curly WEB quote verifies verbatim; check_refs_mirror, check_marks, check_language_zones and citation_sweep are clean for this row, and cluster tiling over Ps.98.1-Ps.101.8 is exact (31 verses expected, 31 covered, 0 problems). I do NOT contest the span: 98:1-3 closes as a completed report of Yahweh's acts, “All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.” (web:Ps.98.3), and 98:4 restarts with a fresh volitive cluster. What fails is the warrant: the row grounds the seam in a register shift to imperative at 98:4 while 98:1 already opens with an imperative, and its rejected_alternative asserts an internal uniformity of grammatical person that neither half has. Two evidence-form defects also stand: a Hebrew quote that overshoots its English gloss into the WEB title pseudo-verse, and an untiered sameness claim against 96:1 that only holds at skeleton tier. Noted but not filed: the quoted 98:1 window straddles a paseq seg (pmarks paseq Ps.98.1 = 1 seg), correctly absent from the quotable bytes and correctly unclaimed; and check_universals flags the row's no-second-label-word statement as an unswept universal, though the claim itself holds against oshb:Ps.98.1 (byte: מִזְמ֡וֹר is the whole superscription before the verse's own content).

challenges.claim: The row's stated seam driver — that the register shifts to imperative at web:Ps.98.4 — is falsified by the plural imperative that already opens web:Ps.98.1, and the rejected_alternative's claim that 98:1-3 and 98:4-9 each stay internally uniform in grammatical person fails on both sides of the seam.
challenges.evidence: Byte-spliced from verse_map_oshb.json (collate: byte tier at every ref cited here). The second word of MT 98:1 is שִׁ֤ירוּ (oshb:Ps.98.1), the same plural-imperative form class as הָרִ֣יעוּ (oshb:Ps.98.4); both witnesses render both as commands — “Sing to Yahweh a new song” (web:Ps.98.1) and “Make a joyful noise to Yahweh, all the earth!” (web:Ps.98.4). Inside the row's own span that imperative is immediately followed by third-person narration, הוֹדִ֣יעַ יְ֭הוָה יְשׁוּעָת֑וֹ (oshb:Ps.98.2). Inside 98:4-9 the imperatives of 98:4-6 (פִּצְח֖וּ וְרַנְּנ֣וּ וְזַמֵּֽרוּ, oshb:Ps.98.4; זַמְּר֣וּ, oshb:Ps.98.5; הָ֝רִ֗יעוּ, oshb:Ps.98.6) give way to third-person prefix forms in 98:7-8 (יִרְעַ֣ם, oshb:Ps.98.7; יִמְחֲאוּ … יְרַנֵּֽנוּ, oshb:Ps.98.8), which WEB renders jussively: “Let the sea roar with its fullness” (web:Ps.98.7) and “Let the rivers clap their hands.” (web:Ps.98.8). Sweep object named first: verses of Ps 98 carrying a 2mp imperative form — 4 VERSES (98:1, 98:4, 98:5, 98:6), so the imperative register straddles the seam rather than beginning at it. No morphology layer exists in the staged extract, so these forms are argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, and re-derive the same way. The span is not contested; the warrant needs replacing with one that survives 98:1.

challenges.claim: Quote/gloss span desync: the byte quote offered for the summons runs from the superscription word, but the English gloss beside it covers only what WEB assigns to web:Ps.98.1, not the title pseudo-verse web:Ps.98.0.
challenges.evidence: The rationale pairs the gloss “Sing to Yahweh a new song” (web:Ps.98.1) with the byte quote מִזְמ֡וֹר שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָ֨ה שִׁ֣יר חָ֭דָשׁ (oshb:Ps.98.1, collate byte). The leading word מִזְמ֡וֹר is what WEB carries as its unnumbered title, “A Psalm.” (web:Ps.98.0) — glossed separately one clause earlier in the same sentence. The Hebrew therefore covers MT 98:1 title-plus-summons while the gloss covers summons only: expansion-without-recut. The recut form is available at zero cost, since שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָ֨ה שִׁ֣יר חָ֭דָשׁ alone is byte-true against oshb:Ps.98.1.

challenges.claim: The signal calls 98:1's opening the same four-word new-song clause as 96:1 inside a byte:-labelled field, but the two clauses agree only at SKELETON tier — they differ at byte and at accent_stripped.
challenges.evidence: Splices: שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָ֨ה שִׁ֣יר חָ֭דָשׁ (oshb:Ps.98.1) against שִׁ֣ירוּ לַ֭יהוָה שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֑שׁ (oshb:Ps.96.1); each is byte-true against its own verse, and neither is byte-true against the other. accent_stripped also separates them, because 98:1 carries a meteg in its divine-name token that 96:1 does not (accent_stripped strips U+0591-05AF only, retaining U+05BD). Agreement holds at skeleton tier: both reduce to the same 5-word consonantal string (skeleton sweep: 2 verses, 96:1 and 98:1). The adjacent row on 98:4-9 states the tier explicitly for the parallel 96:13 comparison; this row should meet the same standard rather than leaving a sameness claim untiered under a byte: label.

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently. All three Hebrew runs collate at BYTE tier against oshb:Ps.98.4, oshb:Ps.98.9 and oshb:Ps.96.13. The rejected_alternative's factual core checks out from bytes: 96:13 carries the doubled clause כִּ֬י בָ֗א כִּ֥י בָא֮ (oshb:Ps.96.13) that 98:9 lacks, and the two verses close on different final words — בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים (oshb:Ps.98.9) against בֶּאֱמוּנָתֽוֹ (oshb:Ps.96.13) — so the row is right that they are not word-for-word. WEB confirms the divergence it names: “He will judge the world with righteousness, the peoples with his truth.” (web:Ps.96.13) against “He will judge the world with righteousness, and the peoples with equity.” (web:Ps.98.9). Its further claim that 98:9's close instead matches 96:10 holds at the WEB-rendering level — “He will judge the peoples with equity.” (web:Ps.96.10) — but not at byte or skeleton tier, where 98:9's closing pair וְ֝עַמִּ֗ים בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים (oshb:Ps.98.9) carries a conjunction that עַ֝מִּ֗ים בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים (oshb:Ps.96.10) lacks; I record that as an observation, not a challenge, because the flanking terms in that sentence are English glosses. check_refs_mirror is clean (96:10 and 96:13 both appear in boundary_evidence_refs), and no mark claim is made. The span 98:4-9 is correct and I do not contest it. Three defects remain: a full-verse Hebrew quote glossed by half a verse, a wrong form label on 98:7-8, and verbatim WEB text set in single curly quotes.

challenges.claim: Quote/gloss span desync at the row's closing citation: the byte quote is the whole of MT 98:9 while the gloss beside it covers only WEB 98:9's second sentence, leaving unglossed exactly the material the row's own rejected_alternative uses to distinguish 98:9 from 96:13.
challenges.evidence: The rationale pairs the gloss “He will judge the world with righteousness, and the peoples with equity.” (web:Ps.98.9) with the byte quote לִֽפְֽנֵי יְהוָ֗ה כִּ֥י בָא֮ לִשְׁפֹּ֪ט הָ֫אָ֥רֶץ יִשְׁפֹּֽט תֵּבֵ֥ל בְּצֶ֑דֶק וְ֝עַמִּ֗ים בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים (oshb:Ps.98.9, collate byte). The gloss corresponds to יִשְׁפֹּֽט תֵּבֵ֥ל בְּצֶ֑דֶק וְ֝עַמִּ֗ים בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים only; the unglossed head לִֽפְֽנֵי יְהוָ֗ה כִּ֥י בָא֮ לִשְׁפֹּ֪ט הָ֫אָ֥רֶץ is rendered “before Yahweh, for he comes to judge the earth.” (web:Ps.98.9). That head is precisely where 96:13 doubles its clause, so the desync suppresses the comparison the row argues two fields later. Either recut the quote to יִשְׁפֹּֽט תֵּבֵ֥ל בְּצֶ֑דֶק וְ֝עַמִּ֗ים בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים or extend the gloss to the whole verse.

challenges.claim: The rationale labels web:Ps.98.7-98.8 cosmic imperatives, but neither verse contains an imperative — all three verbs are third-person prefix forms, and both witnesses treat them as jussives.
challenges.evidence: Byte splices: יִרְעַ֣ם (oshb:Ps.98.7) and יִמְחֲאוּ … יְרַנֵּֽנוּ (oshb:Ps.98.8), all collate byte. Each is a yod-prefix third-person form, not a 2mp imperative; the psalm's actual imperatives are הָרִ֣יעוּ and פִּצְח֖וּ וְרַנְּנ֣וּ וְזַמֵּֽרוּ (oshb:Ps.98.4), זַמְּר֣וּ (oshb:Ps.98.5) and הָ֝רִ֗יעוּ (oshb:Ps.98.6) — 4 verses by sweep (98:4, 98:5, 98:6, plus 98:1 outside this row). WEB agrees: “Let the sea roar with its fullness” (web:Ps.98.7) and “Let the rivers clap their hands.” (web:Ps.98.8) are let-jussives, not commands. The row's own point (addressee widens from congregation to creation) survives; the form word does not.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative says web:Ps.99.4 opens a royal-justice clause addressed in second person, but 99:4 opens in the third person; the first second-person element stands in the verse's second colon.

The row's seam still holds on other grounds, but as written the driver misplaces the person shift by one colon, which matters because the same field uses that shift to defeat an extension through 99:5.

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently. Both Hebrew runs collate at BYTE tier and the row's byte-identity claim between the two refrain instances verifies exactly: קָד֥וֹשׁ הֽוּא (oshb:Ps.99.3) and the closing two words of oshb:Ps.99.5 are the same byte string, so 'collate: 2 verses match at byte tier' is accurate and correctly tiered. All WEB quotes verify verbatim, check_refs_mirror is clean (99:1-3 is carried as a range ref), and no mark claim is made. The span 99:4-5 is defensible and I do not contest it — the refrain bracket is a genuine tier-1 close. But the rejected_alternative's load-bearing warrant is false on the bytes of the row's own seam partner, and check_universals independently flags the same sentence twice (11 claims seen, 4 flags across the cluster, 2 of them here). With that warrant removed the seam rests entirely on the refrain, which is sufficient but is not what the row argues; a confidence of high is not calibrated to a driver that fails on the adjacent verse.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative's claim that 99:1-3 stays third-person throughout is false: MT 99:3 already turns to second-person address of Yahweh with a 2ms pronominal suffix, one verse before the row's seam, so grammatical person cannot carry the 99:3|99:4 boundary.
challenges.evidence: Byte splice from oshb:Ps.99.3 (collate byte): the verse opens יוֹד֣וּ שִׁ֭מְךָ, whose second word carries the 2ms suffix; WEB renders it “Let them praise your great and awesome name.” (web:Ps.99.3). Person distribution across the prior strophe, re-derived verse by verse: 99:1 third person, 99:2 third person, 99:3 SECOND person to Yahweh — 1 of 3 verses, and the one immediately abutting the seam. The rationale's contrast with 'the third-person opening of the prior strophe' survives only because it says opening; the rejected_alternative's 'throughout' does not. The seam itself survives on the byte-identical refrain קָד֥וֹשׁ הֽוּא (oshb:Ps.99.3 / oshb:Ps.99.5), which is the warrant the row should be carrying, and the replacement must pass the test that killed the original.

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently; nothing to contest. The single Hebrew run כִּֽי קָ֝ד֗וֹשׁ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Ps.99.9, and the row's negative claim is exact: it is not byte-identical to קָד֥וֹשׁ הֽוּא (oshb:Ps.99.3 / oshb:Ps.99.5), and the row says so with the tier named rather than asserting a fourth verbatim repetition — the correct handling of the same comparison that the 98:1 row leaves untiered. The ordinal byte-settles before use: refrain returns in Ps 99 are 3 VERSES (99:3, 99:5, 99:9) by splice, so 'third and final' holds. Sweeping the holy root by attested spelling, as the mater hazard requires, the plene form returns 3 VERSES / 3 TOKENS (99:3, 99:5, 99:9) and the defective suffixed form 1 VERSE / 1 TOKEN — that extra token is the construct noun in לְהַ֣ר קָדְשׁ֑וֹ (oshb:Ps.99.9), a different object which the row correctly does not blend into the refrain count. The person claims check out: 99:6-7 are third-person narration and the second-person address at 99:8 is byte-visible in oshb:Ps.99.8. All WEB quotes verify verbatim, including “for Yahweh, our God, is holy!” (web:Ps.99.9). check_refs_mirror is clean — both out-of-span refrain verses 99:3 and 99:5 appear in boundary_evidence_refs. Observation only, no defect: the row could also have noted the inclusio formed by the opening triad רֽוֹמְמ֡וּ יְה֘וָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ (oshb:Ps.99.5), which is byte-identical to the opening triad of oshb:Ps.99.9, and which strengthens rather than threatens the span.

challenges.claim: The plene/defective assignment in the ketiv/qere disclosure is inverted: at MT 101:5 the inline unpointed ketiv is the PLENE spelling and the pointed qere is the DEFECTIVE one, the opposite of what the row states.
challenges.evidence: Byte splices from oshb:Ps.101.5 (collate byte), taken as the first two whitespace tokens of the verse: ketiv מלושני and qere מְלָשְׁנִ֬י. Consonant counts from the skeleton of the same verse: the ketiv token reduces to a 6-letter string carrying the internal waw; the qere token reduces to a 5-letter string with no waw. Plene is the spelling WITH the mater, so the ketiv here is plene and the qere is defective — the row's observed_substrate_signals says the reverse ('the defective ketiv spelling set beside the pointed qere spelling'). The row's sister disclosure at oshb:Ps.100.3 uses the same unpointed-ketiv-first ordering (ולא וְל֣וֹ), confirming the extract convention and so the direction of the error. The final clause, that both spellings are the same word, plene against defective, is correct; only the labels need swapping, and the fix is one word.

challenges.claim: Register violation: the rejected_alternative anchors its parent claim to a positional row reference rather than to a verse.

The available anchor is the psalm's own head, byte: לְדָוִ֗ד מִ֫זְמ֥וֹר (oshb:Ps.101.1) = web:Ps.101.0, which the other Ps 101 row already cites; the repair is a pointer swap and, being a shared-seam fact, should be authored once and installed on both rows.
